In this chapter, it is described that after the departure of Narada Muni, Sage Vyasa Deva sat in deep meditation at his hermitage called Shamyapras, located on the western bank of the Saraswati River, surrounded by bear trees. After purifying himself by touching the water, he entered profound samadhi (spiritual trance). The background of this chapter also includes the incident of Ashwatthama killing Draupadi’s five sons and Arjuna punishing him for that act.
